extracted.intended_audience: U.S. aircraft operators, maintenance/engineering organizations, repair stations, and FAA/inspector compliance staff responsible for implementing Airworthiness Directives (ADs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for operators and maintainers to detect, correct, and mitigate identified unsafe conditions on specified airplane models by following incorporated foreign ADs (EASA/ANAC) with FAA-specific exceptions, compliance times, and approval procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability (airplane models covered)
rubrics_metrics.description: This AD applies to the specified Airbus SAS or Embraer S.A. airplane models certificated in any category as identified in the referenced EASA AD 2024-0097R2 (Airbus) or ANAC AD 1999-02-01R7 (Embraer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AD lists the exact model designations (e.g., Airbus A318/A319/A320/A321 variants; Embraer EMB-145 variants). Operators must determine applicability using those model lists and the referenced IBR material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsafe condition statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD identifies the unsafe condition prompting the rule: for Airbus, cracks on the main landing gear (MLG) door hinge fitting and actuator fitting on the keel beam that could lead to in-flight detachment of an MLG door; for Embraer, cracking or breaking of the rod ends and connecting fittings of the aileron power control actuator (PCA) that could result in reduced controllability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The unsafe-condition description explains the safety risk motivating required inspections and corrective actions and supports the need for compliance within specified times.

rubrics_metrics.name: General compliance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must meet the compliance times set forth in this AD (including those contained in incorporated foreign ADs), except where this AD explicitly provides exceptions or alternate compliance methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference — follow foreign AD procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as specified in AD exceptions, comply with all required actions and compliance times specified in, and in accordance with, the incorporated EASA AD 2024-0097R2 (Airbus) or ANAC AD 1999-02-01R7 (Embraer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The incorporated ADs specify inspection types, intervals, corrective actions, and optional terminating actions; the FAA AD makes those procedures mandatory for U.S. operators except where the FAA AD provides specific deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspections and inspection methods (as specified in incorporated EASA/ANAC ADs)
rubrics_metrics.description: EASA AD 2024-0097R2 specifies repetitive detailed visual, high frequency eddy current (HFEC), and ultrasonic inspections of the MLG door actuator and hinge fittings for discrepancies; ANAC AD specifies repetitive inspections to detect cracking and failure of rod ends and PCA fittings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrective actions identified by those ADs include replacement, modification, and repair. For Airbus, the FAA AD removes the ultrasonic requirement (see exception). The incorporated material determines inspection technique details and intervals unless modified by FAA exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective actions (replacement, modification, repair)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrective actions include replacement of affected fittings, modification of actuator and hinge fittings, and repair of cracks, loose flanged bush, bush migration, wear marks under bolt heads, and other damage; accomplishing the specified modification terminates the repetitive inspections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inspections reveal discrepancies, perform the corrective actions specified in the incorporated AD or use FAA/EASA/DOA-approved repair methods as required by FAA exceptions. On-condition replacement/repair costs are estimated but may be covered by warranty.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAA exceptions to incorporated AD dates and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the incorporated EASA/ANAC ADs refer to specific dates (e.g., effective dates of the foreign AD), this FAA AD requires using the FAA AD's effective date or specified alternate dates (e.g., use April 6, 2015 for certain references to EASA AD 2012-0118).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must substitute the FAA-specified dates in place of the dates cited in the foreign AD when following the incorporated material, per the exception paragraphs in the FAA AD.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAA-required approval path for repairs and instructions from manufacturers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the incorporated AD specifies to 'contact Airbus (or manufacturer) for approved repair instructions', this FAA AD replaces that text with a requirement that 'all repairs must be done before further flight using a method approved by the Manager, AIR-520, Continued Operational Safety Branch, FAA; or EASA; or Airbus SAS’s EASA Design Organization Approval (DOA).' If approved by the DOA, the approval must include the DOA-authorized signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturer instructions alone are not sufficient unless approved through the FAA/EASA/DOA channels specified; this ensures repair methods meet FAA-accepted standards for U.S. operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of referenced inspection tasks with ALS tasks or Service Bulletins (Airbus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where EASA AD 2024-0097R2 references inspection SBs or ALI tasks, this FAA AD replaces those references with explicit allowable alternatives (e.g., ALI task 533154-03-2, 533154-04-2 or 533154-10-1; or Airbus SB A320-53-1195 / A320-53-1325 / A320-53-1196 / A320-53-1326 at any Revision, as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For certain airplane groups (NEO/CEO distinctions), the FAA AD provides transitional language allowing either ALI tasks or Airbus Service Bulletins to be used for initial inspections, with a 3-month transition after the effective date where only the SB may be used thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace/transition period for NEO airplanes (Airbus)
rubrics_metrics.description: FAA added a 3-month grace/transition period for NEO airplanes: for specified airplanes, initial inspections may be done per ALI tasks or Airbus SBs for a three-month transition; after 3 months only the inspection SB may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relief applies only to NEO airplanes (CEO airplanes already subject to prior compliance times). The AD added paragraphs (h)(6) and (h)(7) to effect this transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ultrasonic inspection not required by FAA AD
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the 'Inspection SB 2' in EASA AD 2024-0097R2 specifies to do an ultrasonic inspection in addition to an HFEC inspection, this FAA AD does not require an ultrasonic inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAA added paragraph (h)(8) to clarify that the ultrasonic procedure in certain Airbus SBs is not mandatory under the FAA AD because the NTM does not contain ultrasonic instructions for the referenced SBs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retained maintenance/inspection program revision requirement (Airbus)
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain Airbus airplanes, after the initial inspections and before further flight, revise the maintenance or inspection program to remove Task 533154-02-1 of the Airbus A318/A319/A320/A321 ALS Part 2 (DT ALI) and related documents; the AD actions take precedence over that Task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph restates and carries forward the program revision requirement from AD 2015-02-14 with no changes for specified airplane groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: No FAA reporting requirement (despite foreign AD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the incorporated EASA AD may specify submitting certain information to the manufacturer, this FAA AD does not include that reporting requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators are not required to submit the manufacturer's requested information to comply with the FAA AD, unless another FAA requirement applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMOC (Alternative Methods of Compliance) authority and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manager, AIR-520, Continued Operational Safety Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD if requested using procedures in 14 CFR 39.19. Send requests to your principal inspector or responsible Flight Standards Office, or directly to the manager (email AMOC@faa.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before using any approved AMOC, notify the appropriate principal inspector or the manager of the responsible Flight Standards Office. Follow the procedural requirements in 14 CFR 39.19 when seeking alternate compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of previously approved AMOCs
rubrics_metrics.description: AMOCs approved previously for AD 2015-02-14 are approved as AMOCs for the corresponding provisions of EASA AD 2024-0097R2 that are required by paragraph (g) of this AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides continuity for operators who already have AMOCs in place under the superseded AD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting manufacturer: approved-method requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For any requirement in this AD to obtain instructions from a manufacturer, the instructions must be accomplished using a method approved by the Manager, AIR-520; or EASA; or Airbus SAS’s EASA DOA. If approved by the DOA, the approval must include the DOA-authorized signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures manufacturer-supplied instructions are validated through an authority recognized by the FAA for compliance purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required for Compliance (RC) designation and deviation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If any material contains procedures or tests identified as RC, those procedures and tests must be done to comply with this AD; procedures/tests not identified as RC are recommended. Non-RC procedures may be deviated from using accepted methods in accordance with the operator’s maintenance or inspection program without obtaining an AMOC, provided the RC procedures/tests can be done and the airplane can be returned to an airworthy condition. Any substitutions or changes to RC procedures/tests require AMOC approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must treat RC items as mandatory and obtain AMOC approval for any changes; non-RC items allow limited operator-level flexibility but cannot compromise RC items' completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material incorporated by reference — availability and use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register approved incorporation by reference of specific foreign ADs (EASA AD 2024-0097R2; ANAC AD 1999-02-01R7). Operators must use that material as applicable to do the actions required by this AD unless this AD specifies otherwise. The incorporated material is reasonably available via the addresses provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators are required to consult the full IBR documents to perform inspections, tests, and corrective actions; the FAA provides contact and access information (EASA, ANAC, FAA, and NARA) for obtaining the IBR material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embraer-specific exceptions to ANAC AD (dates, paragraphs, and terminology)
rubrics_metrics.description: This FAA AD for Embraer replaces certain references in ANAC AD 1999-02-01R7 (e.g., where ANAC refers to '21 jul. 2004,' use November 8, 2006); the FAA AD does not adopt paragraph (f) of the ANAC AD; and it replaces 'operating days' with 'days' where specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators following the incorporated ANAC AD must apply these FAA-specified textual and timing substitutions when complying in the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embraer: mandatory before-further-flight replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where ANAC AD specifies replacing cracked and failed rod ends and PCA fittings, for this FAA AD all applicable replacements must be done before further flight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This tightens compliance by requiring immediate grounding until replacement is complete when cracked/failed components are found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embraer: initial inspection compliance times by PCA part number
rubrics_metrics.description: If PCA P/N is 394900-1003 or 394900-1005, do the initial inspection within 3 days after Nov 8, 2006; if P/N 394900-1007, within 14 days after Nov 8, 2006; for other listed P/Ns with new reinforced fittings, within 500 flight hours after Nov 8, 2006.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AD specifies different initial-compliance windows tied to PCA part numbers to address risk differences among hardware variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embraer: compliance times for installation of reinforcements/new fittings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where ANAC required an installation within '6000 operating cycles,' this FAA AD specifies compliance times depending on PCA P/N: either before 6,000 total flight hours or within a short window after Nov 8, 2006, or for other P/Ns before 6,000 total flight cycles or within 600 flight cycles after Nov 8, 2006, whichever occurs later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific numeric thresholds for flight hours/cycles and short after-effective-date windows are provided to ensure timely installation of terminating modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embraer: acceptable methods for prior and future inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspections performed before the FAA AD effective date using AMM Task 27-12-01-212-002-A00 or an FAA/ANAC-approved method are acceptable; inspections on or after the effective date must be done using the task identified in ANAC AD 1999-02-01R7 or using a method approved as specified in the AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides continuity for past inspections while ensuring future inspections conform to the post-AD task numbering/approved methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embraer: initial inspection timing relative to installation/reinforcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where ANAC specified to accomplish the initial inspection 'in conjunction with the new PCA fittings and reinforcement provisions,' this FAA AD requires accomplishing the initial inspection within 500 flight hours after accomplishing the installation and reinforcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a clear numeric window (500 flight hours) after modification during which the first inspection must occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embraer: inspection interval wording (maximum-interval requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where ANAC specified 'every 500 flight hours' or 'every 1000 flight hours,' this FAA AD replaces that wording with 'at intervals not to exceed 500 flight hours' and 'at intervals not exceeding 1,000 flight hours,' respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'not to exceed' phrasing emphasizes maximum interval between inspections rather than prescribing strict periodicity language, making compliance interpretation explicit.
